title: Fast Thermalization With Quantum Algorithms
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 03 July 2026;
tldr: A quantum algorithm efficiently prepares thermal equilibrium states, advancing quantum simulation.
motivation: Preparing thermal states is crucial for quantum simulation but computationally hard; this work provides an efficient algorithm for an important class of thermal states.
method: The algorithm leverages quantum signal processing and Hamiltonian simulation to prepare Gibbs states with provable efficiency.
result: The algorithm achieves polynomial scaling in system size and inverse temperature, outperforming classical methods.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that thermalization can be accelerated using quantum algorithms, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and simulation.

title: Learning Pure Quantum States Almost Without Regret
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper develops a regret-minimizing online learning algorithm for pure quantum states, achieving near-optimal sample complexity.
motivation: Learning unknown quantum states efficiently is fundamental to quantum information processing, but existing methods often require many copies or assume prior knowledge. The authors aim to design an algorithm that learns pure states with minimal regret in an online setting.
method: The authors propose a Bayesian approach using a Dirichlet prior over the Bloch sphere and update beliefs via sequential measurements. They derive a regret bound by analyzing the information gain and using a novel concentration inequality for quantum measurements.
result: The algorithm achieves a regret of O(√T) for T rounds, matching the lower bound up to logarithmic factors, and outperforms previous methods in numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and theoretically optimal online learning algorithm for pure quantum states, with implications for quantum tomography and adaptive quantum metrology.

result: They demonstrate significant improvements in gate fidelity and reduction of crosstalk compared to standard methods, enabling high-fidelity multi-qubit operations.

title: Enhancing Classical Simulation With Noisy Quantum Devices
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 July 2026;

result: They demonstrate that the hybrid approach can achieve higher simulation fidelity than purely classical methods for certain circuit sizes and noise levels.
conclusion: Noisy quantum devices can be valuable tools for enhancing classical simulation, offering a practical intermediate step before fault-tolerant quantum computers are available.

title: A Context-aware Gate Set Tomography: Improving The Self-consistent Characterization Of Trapped-ion Universal Gate Sets By Leveraging non-Markovianity
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper introduces a context-aware gate set tomography method that leverages non-Markovianity to improve the self-consistent characterization of trapped-ion universal gate sets.
motivation: Standard gate set tomography assumes Markovian noise, which is inaccurate for trapped-ion systems where non-Markovian effects degrade characterization accuracy. The authors aim to develop a more realistic tomography framework that accounts for these effects.
method: The authors propose a context-aware gate set tomography protocol that models non-Markovian noise by incorporating temporal correlations in the error processes. They apply this to trapped-ion universal gate sets and compare with standard GST.
result: The context-aware method yields significantly improved fidelity estimates and error bars compared to standard GST, demonstrating that leveraging non-Markovianity enhances self-consistent characterization.
conclusion: Accounting for non-Markovianity in gate set tomography is crucial for accurate characterization of trapped-ion quantum processors, and the proposed method provides a practical improvement over existing techniques.

title: A Framework Of Partial Error Correction For Intermediate-scale Quantum Computers
